newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Foreign interest underpins Swedish crown, yields.
newsitem.headline: Foreign interest underpins Swedish crown, yields.

text.p: Swedish long debt yields and the crown were slightly stronger at midday on Friday on interest from foreign investors.
The rest of the session would be quiet because of the U.S. independence day holiday.

"U.S. funds bought Swedish bonds yesterday. Traders were short today and needed to buy," one dealer said. Foreign investors have been more positive about Sweden lately. "What we have seen today is a confirmation of that," one dealer said.
Technical levels for ten-year bonds have been broken and technically have entered unknown territory, dealers said.
The spread between Italian and German ten-year bonds decreased. This could also have helped Sweden today.

The spread between Swedish and German longer yields fell four basis points to 87. The Swedish ten-year bond yield inched down three basis points to 6.48 percent while the six-month T-bill rates fell one basis point to 4.09 percent.

The crown gained to 4.4015 against the mark from 4.4095 late Thursday. Interest from U.S. investors was behind the strength in the crown, dealers said. The crown was likely to trade between 4.3940 and 4.4030 today, one dealer said.
